verdict.headline: Harvest provides self-serve OAuth2 application registration via Harvest ID with immediate access.
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: 10–15 minutes to register an application in Harvest ID and complete code flow.
verdict.timeToProduction: Immediate upon developer setup; no external app review process is documented.
verdict.handsOnEffort: Minimal: fill out application registration form in Harvest ID and handle standard OAuth2 authorization code exchange.
verdict.biggestRisk: Missing mandatory headers like User-Agent or attempting admin operations without requisite account roles returns 403 or 400 errors.

ownAppDecision.summary: You can use Composio managed auth to skip setup, but creating your own OAuth app is simple and self-serve if custom branding or direct client secrets are preferred.
reasons: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Harvest for fast prototyping.
Registering your own app gives custom branding on the consent screen and direct control of OAuth credentials.

requirements.detail: Required to access the Developers section in Harvest ID and register an OAuth2 Client.
Every API request must include a descriptive User-Agent header (e.g., MyApp (email@example.com)).

permissions.name: harvest:{ACCOUNT_ID} / harvest:all
permissions.purpose: Access time tracking, users, projects, and approvals within Harvest accounts.
permissions.notes: Permissions inherit directly from the authorizing user's account role and custom permissions.

permissions.name: forecast:{ACCOUNT_ID} / forecast:all
permissions.purpose: Access scheduling and project planning data in Forecast.
permissions.notes: Granted when Forecast product scope is enabled and authorized by user.

nuances.title: User-Agent Header Requirement
nuances.detail: Omitting a User-Agent header causes API calls to fail with 400 Bad Request.

nuances.title: Role-Based API Restrictions
nuances.detail: Resource access is tied to the authorizing user's role; non-admins receive 403 Forbidden on privileged endpoints.

nuances.title: Multi-Account Request Routing
nuances.detail: Multi-account applications must send the Harvest-Account-Id header on requests to specify target account context.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 400 Bad Request with body 'User-Agent header required'
blockers.howToProceed: Add a descriptive User-Agent header containing application name and contact email to all outbound requests.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 403 Forbidden when calling restricted endpoints like /v2/permissions or billable rates
blockers.howToProceed: Ensure the authorizing user has the necessary Admin or Manager role within the target Harvest account.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 403 Forbidden with message 'Timesheet approvals are not enabled for this company'
blockers.howToProceed: Enable timesheet approvals in the target Harvest company settings prior to calling approvals endpoints.
